seo.title: Factors of 60 Speed Grid - Clock & Geometry Number Theory
seo.metaDescription: Click all 12 factors of 60 on a 100-number grid. Explore the ancient sexagesimal base number used in clocks and angles in this speed clicker.
seo.intro: The number 60 was chosen by ancient Babylonian astronomers as the foundation of timekeeping and geometry (60 seconds in a minute, 60 minutes in an hour, 360 degrees in a circle) specifically because it has an extraordinary number of factors. Sixty has 12 positive divisors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, and 60. Locating all 12 factors requires comprehensive mental math across multiple times tables.
seo.howToPlay: Locate and click all 12 factors of 60 across the 100-number grid. Correct selections lock green with a checkmark. Incorrect tiles flash red and deduct 2 seconds. Discover all 12 factors before time runs out.
seo.teacherNotes: Share the history of 60 with students. Explain why a clock face can be divided evenly into halves, thirds, fourths, fifths, and sixths without awkward fractions.

faq.q: Why did ancient civilizations use base 60?
faq.a: Because 60 can be divided evenly by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, making division of time and trade goods exceptionally simple.
